questions.question: Does EscrowService's new duplicate-fund-attempt guard (F-0873) correctly block EVERY scenario where money for the same campaign/milestone scope is already secured or being secured, not just PENDING/FUNDED?
questions.why_it_matters: A gap here is a double-debit bug -- the exact class of defect F-0873 was written to close. If a fund attempt lands while the only existing hold for that scope is in a state the new check doesn't recognize as 'active', the brand's wallet can be debited twice for one campaign/milestone.
questions.answer: No -- there is a real gap, though a narrow one. `EscrowService.ACTIVE_HOLD_STATUSES` (new) = {PENDING, FUNDED} only. `EscrowStatus.FROZEN` (a disputed hold -- real, currently-secured money, per AdminBrandService.java:695-703's own comment 'FUNDED (locked), RELEASED (paid out), or FROZEN (disputed but still real money)' and DeliverableCleanupJob.java:70-75's 'FULL unreleased escrow set' = {FUNDED, FROZEN, PENDING}) is excluded from the new dedup check's active set. A fresh initiateFund attempt (reload/retry, fresh idempotency key) for a campaign/milestone scope whose only existing hold is FROZEN will NOT find it via `findActiveByCampaignIdAndMilestoneId(... , {PENDING,FUNDED})`, and will proceed to create a second hold and debit the wallet again for money that is already held (just disputed). EscrowServiceTest's 4 new F-0873 tests only exercise PENDING/FUNDED-scoped dedup and the campaign-level vs milestone-level scoping; none constructs a FROZEN pre-existing hold for this path.
questions.evidence: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/EscrowService.java: new `ACTIVE_HOLD_STATUSES = EnumSet.of(PENDING, FUNDED)` (javadoc explicitly reasons about RELEASED/REFUNDED but never mentions FROZEN); cross-checked EscrowStatus's 5 real values (PENDING, FUNDED, RELEASED, REFUNDED, FROZEN) and confirmed FROZEN's semantics as 'real, currently-secured, disputed money' via AdminBrandService.java and DeliverableCleanupJob.java, both of which explicitly group FROZEN with FUNDED as still-real escrow. `grep FROZEN influora-api/src/test/java/com/influora/service/EscrowServiceTest.java` shows FROZEN only exercised in freeze/dispute-settlement tests, never in the F-0873 dedup tests.
questions.remaining_uncertainty: Whether this is reachable in practice depends on operational sequencing: a hold typically only becomes FROZEN after it was first FUNDED (i.e., already funded once, then disputed) -- for a NEW fund attempt to race against a FROZEN hold, someone would have to retry/reload a funding action for a scope that is currently under dispute, which may be rare. Did not attempt to reproduce with a live/integration test (would require constructing a disputed hold and then a second concurrent fund call), so this is code-reading (E2) only, not runtime-confirmed.

questions.question: When F-0857/F-0858's delta-charge fires a SECOND platform-fee charge on the same campaign (a paused campaign resumed after its budget was raised), does the brand's statutory commission invoice reflect the additional amount actually charged?
questions.why_it_matters: This is a real money movement (a second, real PLATFORM_FEE wallet debit) paired with a compliance document (GST commission invoice) that is supposed to correspond to it. A silent mismatch is a tax/audit-trail defect, not just a UX rough edge.
questions.answer: No. `CommissionInvoiceService.createBrandLegAtPublish` (unchanged by this delta) does `var existing = invoiceRepository.findByCampaignIdAndLeg(campaign.getId(), BRAND); if (existing.isPresent()) return existing.get();` BEFORE doing anything else -- so a second call for the same campaign (which BrandCampaignFeeService.chargeOnPublish now makes on a delta top-up) is a complete no-op: it returns the FIRST invoice, for the FIRST (smaller) amount, unchanged. The wallet ledger will show two real PLATFORM_FEE debits for that campaign; the on-file invoice will show only the first. This is self-disclosed in BrandCampaignFeeService.java's own new javadoc comment ('a SECOND (delta) charge on the same campaign is a no-op there today... out of scope here; flagged to Swapnil') -- i.e. a known, accepted, NOT-YET-RULED-ON gap being shipped alongside the fix that creates the scenario where it first becomes reachable (before this delta, chargeOnPublish could only ever be called once per campaign in practice, so this dedup was previously unreachable dead code, not a live gap).

questions.question: Does the two-step publish UI (SecureAndPublishStep, shared by CampaignForm, BrandNewHypeCampaignPage and BrandCampaignDetailPage) correctly prevent double-funding and double-publishing under double-click / reload, and does it behave consistently across all three call sites?
questions.why_it_matters: This is the money-moving UI surface for the whole F-0848 rewrite; a double-click here means a duplicate wallet debit, and an inconsistency between the three call sites means the same conceptual action (resume a paused-but-already-funded campaign) is handled two different ways depending on which screen the brand is on.
questions.answer: Double-click/double-submit protection is present and test-covered on all three surfaces (a ref-gated in-flight flag in CampaignForm.handleSubmit, BrandNewHypeCampaignPage.submit, and SecureAndPublishStep.publish itself, independent of React's disabled-render timing). However, the three call sites are NOT fully consistent for the PAUSED-with-existing-funds case: BrandCampaignDetailPage explicitly branches on `campaign.status === 'DRAFT'` to route into SecureAndPublishStep, and resumes a PAUSED campaign directly via `handleToggleCampaignStatus('ACTIVE')` WITHOUT the step at all (confirmed by its own new F-0874 test: 'a PAUSED campaign (funds already secured) still shows Resume Campaign and resumes directly -- no secure-the-funds step'). CampaignForm and BrandNewHypeCampaignPage have no such branch -- editing ANY existing campaign (DRAFT or PAUSED) and pressing Publish/Launch always routes through SecureAndPublishStep with `checkExistingFunds=true`, which for an already-funded PAUSED campaign just adds one extra 'Publish campaign' confirm click rather than resuming immediately. Functionally safe (no double-fund), but it means the exact same user action ('resume a paused, already-funded campaign') takes a different number of clicks and shows different UI depending on which of the three screens the brand is using.

findings.title: EscrowService's new duplicate-fund-attempt guard (F-0873) does not treat a FROZEN (disputed) hold as 'active', unlike the rest of the codebase
findings.evidence: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/EscrowService.java new `ACTIVE_HOLD_STATUSES = EnumSet.of(PENDING, FUNDED)`, used by the new duplicate-fund dedup check. EscrowStatus has 5 values (PENDING, FUNDED, RELEASED, REFUNDED, FROZEN). Two OTHER, unrelated, already-committed pieces of this codebase explicitly treat FROZEN as real, currently-secured money for the exact same kind of 'is this scope's money still held' question: AdminBrandService.java:695-703 ('Escrow money that floors a budget cut: FUNDED (locked), RELEASED (paid out), or FROZEN (disputed but still real money)') and DeliverableCleanupJob.java:70-75 ('the FULL unreleased escrow set... FROZEN = disputed/held money' -> Set.of(FUNDED, FROZEN, PENDING)).
findings.impact: A fresh initiateFund call (reload/retry with a new idempotency key) targeting a campaign/milestone scope whose only existing hold is currently FROZEN (i.e., was funded, then disputed) will not be recognized as already having money secured, and would proceed to create a second EscrowHold and debit the workspace wallet a second time for that scope.
findings.recommended_fix: Add EscrowStatus.FROZEN to ACTIVE_HOLD_STATUSES in EscrowService.java (or explicitly document why FROZEN is deliberately excluded here, if there is a reason this reviewer did not find -- e.g. if a FROZEN hold is scoped only at the milestone/collaboration level and can never coexist with a fresh campaign-level fund attempt for the same milestone id, which was not confirmed either way).
findings.verification_required: A new EscrowServiceTest case: construct a FROZEN hold for a campaign/milestone scope, call initiateFund again for the same scope with a fresh idempotency key, and assert it either returns the existing hold (matching the PENDING/FUNDED contract) or is explicitly and intentionally rejected some other way -- currently neither happens; it silently creates a second hold.

findings.title: F-0857/F-0858's new delta-charge path can produce a second real PLATFORM_FEE wallet debit with NO corresponding update to the brand's GST commission invoice (self-disclosed, unresolved)
